holidays.name: International Talk Like a Pirate Day
holidays.description: Every September 19, landlubbers everywhere swap "hello" for "ahoy," sprinkle their sentences with "arrr," and dress up like swashbuckling sea rovers. Offices, restaurants, and schools join in, and some businesses even offer pirate-themed freebies for anyone who plays along.
holidays.origin: The day began in 1995, when two friends, John Baur and Mark Summers, came up with it during a racquetball game. It spread widely after humorist Dave Barry wrote about it in his newspaper column in 2002.
holidays.funFact: The date, September 19, was picked because it was the birthday of one of the founders' ex-wives, so it was easy to remember.

holidays.name: National Butterscotch Pudding Day
holidays.description: This is a day for spooning up silky, brown-sugar-and-butter pudding. Butterscotch is the caramel-like cousin that often gets overlooked, so today it gets its own turn to shine. Eat it plain, layer it in parfaits, or top it with whipped cream.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance with no clearly documented founder. It celebrates a classic dessert that has been popular since the late 1800s.
holidays.funFact: Despite the name, butterscotch has no Scotch whisky in it. It is made from butter and brown sugar.
